Relative Squared Error of Imputation Methods Against a Null Baseline

Source: R/imputation_rse.R
compare_imputation_rse.Rd

Scores imputation methods on cells whose true value is known (values you masked, then imputed). For each variable and method it computes the root mean squared error, the RMSE of a **null baseline** that predicts every cell with one overall value, and the **relative squared error** $$\mathrm{RSE} = (\mathrm{RMSE}_{\mathrm{method}} / \mathrm{RMSE}_{\mathrm{null}})^2.$$ An RSE below 1 beats the null baseline, 1 matches it, above 1 is worse.

Usage

compare_imputation_rse(
  results_df,
  null_method = c("mean", "median"),
  baseline = NULL,
  variable_col = "variable",
  method_col = "method",
  truth_col = "truth",
  imputed_col = "imputed"
)

Arguments

results_df

A data frame with one row per scored cell, with the columns named by `variable_col`, `method_col`, `truth_col` and `imputed_col`. Cells with a missing truth or imputed value are dropped and counted in `n_dropped`. Alternatively, a table that already has `rmse` and `null_rmse` columns per variable and method.

null_method

`"mean"` (default) or `"median"`.

baseline

Optional baseline values; see Null baseline.

variable_col, method_col, truth_col, imputed_col

Column names in `results_df`.

Value

A tibble of class `cbe_rse` with `variable`, `method`, `n`, `n_dropped`, `rmse`, `null_rmse`, `rse`, ordered by variable and RSE. Extra columns named `pct_miss` are kept.

Null baseline

By default the baseline value is the mean (or median) of the held-out `truth` values of that variable (every row of `results_df` for the variable counts once), one value per variable shared by all methods. This is an **oracle** baseline: it uses the very values being predicted, so it is the best constant for the mean (it minimises the RMSE) and a method that imputes the training mean scores an RSE slightly above 1. (The median minimises the absolute error, not the RMSE.) Note that [tune_impute_numeric()] defines its RSE differently, with the mean of the unmasked training values as the baseline, so its `mean` method scores exactly 1. To use the training data's mean or median here as well, pass `baseline`: a named numeric vector (names are variables) or a data frame with `variable` and `value`. If the null RMSE is 0 (all truths equal the baseline) the RSE is `NA`. RSEs of different methods are only comparable when they were scored on the same cells; the function warns when the cell counts differ.

See also

[tbl_best_imputation_method()], [plot_rse_by_column()], [plot_rse_vs_missingness()], [build_best_imputed_data()], [tune_impute_numeric()]

Examples

set.seed(1)
cells <- data.frame(
  variable = "x", truth = rnorm(40, 10, 2)
)
res <- rbind(
  transform(cells, method = "mean", imputed = 10),
  transform(cells, method = "good", imputed = truth + rnorm(40, 0, 0.5))
)
compare_imputation_rse(res)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   variable method     n n_dropped  rmse null_rmse    rse
#>   <chr>    <chr>  <int>     <int> <dbl>     <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 x        good      40         0 0.461      1.75 0.0693
#> 2 x        mean      40         0 1.76       1.75 1.01
